name: English
_purpose: Every word scripts/check.py and scripts/card.py say to a person. Keys starting with _ are notes for translators. Keep every {placeholder} as it is. A missing key falls back to this file.
place_home_says: Claude Code is sitting in your home folder, not in a work folder.
place_home_do: Make or open a work folder and start there. The trust question that a remote session needs is never remembered for the home folder.
version_unknown_says: Could not ask Claude Code for its version.
version_unknown_do: Open a new terminal window and try again. If the word claude is not found there either, Claude Code is installed somewhere this terminal does not look.
version_old_says: Claude Code {ver} is older than this evening needs.
version_old_do: Update Claude Code, then run this check again.
remote_off_says: {name} is set in {where}: the remote will not work while it is.
killer_hard_do: Remote Control needs the setting that this switches off. Unset it where it is set, then start Claude Code again.
killer_soft_fine_says: {name} is set in {where}. On Claude Code {ver} that alone does not stop the remote.
killer_soft_fine_do: It does stop it if your organization requires Trusted Devices. If yours does, unset it where it is set; run this check with --trusted-devices and it is counted as a stop.
killer_soft_trusted_do: Your organization requires Trusted Devices, and with this set the remote does not come up. Unset it where it is set, then start Claude Code again.
killer_soft_old_do: A Claude Code older than 2.1.283, or one whose version could not be read, turns the remote off when this is set. Update Claude Code, or unset it where it is set.
redirect_do: The remote works only against Anthropic's own address, not through a gateway or proxy. Unset it and start Claude Code again. If your company requires the gateway, the phone reaches this machine by branch C in the ready skill (SSH and tmux over Tailscale), and cloud sessions (branch B) still work once you sign in with claude auth login.
api_key_do: The remote runs on a claude.ai sign-in (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise), not on an API key. Unset it where it is set and sign in with /login. If your company gives you only a key, the phone reaches this machine by branch C in the ready skill (SSH and tmux over Tailscale), or through a channel such as Telegram, which works with a Console key.
other_cloud_do: The remote and cloud sessions need Anthropic's own service; through Bedrock, Google Cloud or Microsoft Foundry they are not offered. If you also have a claude.ai seat, unset it for this session. If the company keeps all of it in its own cloud, the phone reaches this machine by branch C in the ready skill: SSH and tmux over Tailscale, with Blink or Termius on the phone.
refusal_do: Someone, possibly a past you, turned the remote off in writing. Set it to false or remove the line.
refusal_managed_do: Your IT administrator turned the remote off on this computer, and nothing in your own files overrides that. Cloud sessions (branch B in the ready skill) have no per-computer switch, and branch C needs none.
quiet_ok_says: Nothing on this machine is quietly switching the remote off.
channels_on_says: Channels: your organization's policy on this computer allows them ({plugins}).
channels_off_says: Channels: your organization's policy on this computer does not turn them on.
channels_off_do: Only needed to reach this machine through Telegram, Discord or iMessage. An Owner turns them on at claude.ai, Admin settings, Claude Code, Channels; or IT sets channelsEnabled to true in managed settings, with allowedChannelPlugins naming the ones allowed.
sleep_never_says: On mains power this Mac does not go to sleep by itself.
sleep_after_says: On mains power this Mac sleeps after {minutes} {unit}.
sleep_after_do: Set sleep to Never for mains power in System Settings, and leave the lid open: the work runs exactly as long as the machine is awake, and reconnects by itself the moment it wakes.
sleep_unread_says: Could not read this Mac's sleep setting.
sleep_unread_do: Check System Settings and set sleep to Never while on mains power.
sleep_windows_says: On Windows the sleep setting lives in Power & sleep.
sleep_windows_do: Open Power & sleep settings, set both screen and sleep to Never while plugged in, and leave the lid open.
sleep_other_says: On this system the sleep setting lives in its power settings.
sleep_other_do: Turn off automatic sleep while the machine is on mains power.
out_missing_do: Make a folder called {out} inside a folder your phone can already see (the one your cloud drive syncs). Everything finished goes there as a file.
rule_ok_says: The handover rule is in CLAUDE.md.
rule_missing_says: CLAUDE.md does not mention the handover rule.
rule_missing_do: Add two lines to CLAUDE.md: everything finished is written to a file in {out}/ with a one-line summary on the first line, and the answer in the conversation stays short enough to read on a phone.
sync_none_says: Found no folder on this machine that a phone also sees.
sync_none_do: This is how a photo taken in town reaches the work at home. Make a folder in Google Drive or Dropbox, put the same app on the phone, and run this check again with --shared and the folder. Not iCloud Drive if the phone you carry is an Android one: iCloud has no app there.
sync_absent_says: The shared folder {folder} is not here.
sync_absent_do: Anything the phone puts in a folder by that name goes nowhere you will find it. Open the drive's app, read the folder's real name, and run this check again with --shared and that name.
sync_empty_says: {where}: {folder} — empty, so there is no date to show you.
sync_test_do: One photo proves the drive is carrying this folder to your phone, and it takes a second before you leave: put one photo in from the phone and watch the line above change. If it stays the same, the sync is stuck - fix it now, at home, not in town.
sync_icloud_do: And this is iCloud Drive, which has no Android app at all: if the phone in your pocket is an Android one, choose Google Drive or Dropbox instead.
sync_unknown_do: Nothing on this machine says this folder is shared with anything — it may be an ordinary folder that only this computer can see. Check in the drive's own app that this is the folder it syncs.
report_title: POCKETCALL — is this machine ready to be left alone?
report_bad: {bad} of {total} not ready. Fix those, then run this again.
report_ready: All ready. The remote itself is turned on with /remote-control, and the phone joins by scanning the code it shows.
report_look_yourself: What you look at yourself, and the leave skill says how: that you are signed in on the phone, that notifications are allowed there, whether the shared folder is really syncing at this minute (one test photo), how much of your allowance is left, and on a Team or Enterprise plan that an Owner has turned the remote on for the organization.
card_shared_unknown: the one your drive syncs and your phone can open
card_saved: Saved to {path}. Print it. A card on the wall beats a file you will not open.
card: POCKETCALL — the card
Written {date}. Keep it where you can see it, not where you file it.
WHAT THE PHONE CAN DO while the work runs on your computer
See the same conversation, as it happens.
Send a new task, and it starts now.
Answer the question it asks you.
Say yes or no when it asks permission.
Send a photo or a file from the phone, with or without a note.
FIVE THINGS THAT KEEP THE EVENING ALIVE
The computer stays awake: it works exactly as long as it is awake.
Finished documents come back as files: everything finished goes into
{out}/, and you open it with your normal phone app.
The modes that act without asking are switched on at your desk, on purpose.
The allowance is watched at the desk: when it runs out, the phone simply goes quiet.
A shared folder that stopped syncing goes quiet too - the photo you send stays on
the phone, looking sent. One test photo before you leave proves it carries.
THIRTY SECONDS AT THE DOOR — say these five out loud, every time you go
1. Plugged in. A battery that runs out is a computer switched off, and from town you
cannot plug it back in.
2. Lid open, sleep set to never. A closed lid is sleep, and sleep is a stop.
3. The window with the work in it stays open. Close it and the phone goes dark in seconds.
4. The shared folder is there: {shared}
That is where a photo you take in town lands, and where finished work comes back.
This computer worked that path out by itself. If it is not the folder you use, cross
it out and write yours in with a pen — the card is yours, not the computer's.
5. Phone in your hand before the door, not after it: signed in as you, notifications
allowed, one message sent from where you are standing and one answer back.
If all five are true, the evening works. Saying them out loud is the point: a person who
says "plugged in" looks at the cable, and a person who reads it does not.
IF THE PHONE GOES QUIET
It is one of four things, in this order of likelihood:
the computer went to sleep · the window was closed · the allowance ran out ·
the phone silenced the notification (focus mode, battery saver).
None of them is a fault of yours, and none of them loses your work.
DO NOT APPROVE ON THE PHONE WHAT YOU CANNOT SEE
If the request does not say which file, what happens to it and whether it can be
undone, the answer is no, or "wait until I am at the desk". Nothing is lost by waiting.
YOUR SIGN-IN STAYS YOURS
Never sign in to your Claude account inside some other company's app or site that
offers you a remote. Handing over your sign-in is against the terms, and the ones that
ask for it are the ones you should walk away from. The remote you are using is the one
that came with what you already pay for.
WHAT IS STORED WHERE
While the remote is on, the conversation is kept on the company's servers so that all
your screens can show the same thing. Your files stay on your computer, and the work is
done there. Those are two different things, and only the first one leaves the house.
approve_title: Claude Code asks for your decision
approve_cut: Too long to read in full here, so there is no Yes: answer No, or at the desk.
approve_in_file: The whole card is in the file: the command, every file and the diff.
remote_paired: Paired. Open this link on the phone and add it to the home screen:
remote_telegram: Telegram is set: approval cards go to your chat, and only the people you allowed can press the buttons.
remote_not_paired: This computer is not paired yet: remote.py pair --relay <address>, or remote.py telegram.
remote_away: Away: permission questions go to the phone.
remote_back: At the desk: questions stay on this screen, no cards, no push.
remote_off: The pairing is forgotten on this computer.
remote_joined: This computer joined the phone's pairing: it reads the notes from the phone and sends its cards to the same phone.
remote_bad_link: That is not a phone link from remote.py pair: it carries no key after #k=.
_task: Lines for scripts/task.py: a voice note becomes a task in the company's tracker, a session opens a pull request, and the phone approves it. The footer lines are written under each task in the tracker, read by the whole team; the card heading is the first line on the phone; the declined line is a comment on the pull request. The held, moved and checks lines answer a Yes the desk could not carry out at once and reassure the person that nothing merged behind their back; the start-again lines tell the phone a session is tried again.
task_label: Filed from the phone by Pocketcall
task_from_voice: a voice note in the session
task_setup_done: Tasks go to {where}; pull requests are looked for in {repo}.
task_setup_routine: Cloud tasks go to your routine: its saved prompt carries out the task in the routine-fire-payload block.
task_no_tracker: No tracker is set yet: task.py setup --github <owner/name>, or task.py setup --webhook <address> --repo <owner/name>.
task_bad_repo: {repo} is not owner/name, the way GitHub writes a repository.
task_no_words: No words to file: put them after file, give --from <file>, or send them on standard input.
task_need_gh: This step runs the GitHub CLI: install it from cli.github.com and sign in once with gh auth login.
task_webhook_failed: The tracker's address did not take it: {why}
task_need_claude: Starting a session runs Claude Code here: the claude command, signed in.
task_no_session_link: no link to a session came within {seconds} seconds
task_start_again: {why} The desk tries again in {minutes} min.
task_not_started: {why} After {tries} tries the desk stops; task.py start <task> --cloud tries again.
task_no_folder: {folder} is not a folder on this computer: task.py setup --folder <a checkout of the repository>.
task_git_failed: git did not make the branch for the task: {why}
task_unknown: No task {key} in this computer's record or in the tracker.
task_started_cloud: A cloud session took this task; it opens a pull request when the change is ready. {session}
task_started_home: A session on {host} took this task, on the branch {branch}.
task_no_change: The session finished without changing a file. What it said: {said}
task_stopped: The session on {host} stopped before a pull request: {why}. Its worktree stays at {tree}.
task_pr_said: What the session says it did:
task_pr_closed: {url} is no longer open: there is nothing to approve.
task_card_heading: A pull request waits for your Yes: {title}
task_card_heading_by: A pull request by {author} waits for your Yes: {title}
task_card_heading_fork: A pull request from a fork, by {author}, waits for your Yes: {title}
task_card_sent: The card for {url} is on the phone.
task_card_waiting: No answer from the phone in time: the pull request waits on GitHub, and task.py card sends its card again.
task_review: Yes from the phone, on a card that showed every file and the whole diff at commit {sha}.
task_declined: Declined from the phone. The pull request stays open; a new commit brings a new card.
task_merge_refused: The phone said Yes and GitHub did not merge: {why}
task_held: Yes from the phone is kept for commit {sha}: it merges the moment the checks the repository requires have passed. {url}
task_held_desk: The Yes stays kept for that commit: task.py watch on this computer merges it the moment the checks pass.
task_moved: A newer commit is on {url}, so this Yes merges nothing: that commit's own card comes next.
task_checks_failed: The checks the repository requires did not pass on {url}, so nothing was merged: a fix brings a new commit and a new card.
task_note_unread: This note did not open with this pairing's key, so it was not filed.
task_note_failed: The tracker did not take this note: {why}. Your words: {words}
task_watching: The desk is on: notes from the phone become tasks{start}, and every pull request for a task comes to the phone as a card. Ctrl-C stops it.
task_watching_cloud: , each handed to a cloud session
task_watching_home: , each done by a session on this computer
task_desk_elsewhere: Another desk on this phone is on: this one waits, and takes over when that one stops.
task_list_empty: No tasks in this computer's record yet.
board_empty: No jobs on the board: a Claude Code session, a night run or a review appears here the moment it starts.
board_page_stamp: Updated {time}; the page refreshes itself every minute.
board_page_set: The board page is {path}: open it on the phone from that folder, it is rewritten at every change.
board_page_off: The board page is no longer written.
board_page_no_folder: No folder at {folder}: give the shared folder the phone already sees.
board_ring_bad: An ntfy address starts with https:// - for example https://ntfy.sh/<your topic>.
board_ring_test: Pocketcall board: the phone rings when a job waits for you, is done, or rests on a limit.
board_when_away: they ring while you are away (remote.py away)
board_when_never: they never ring, the board and its page stay up to date
board_cleared: Finished jobs are off the board.
board_run_needs: Give the command after --, for example: board.py run --name tests -- npm test
steer_stopped: Stop sent to {job}: it ends after the step it is on.
steer_no_folder: {job} has no task folder to steer: Continue and Stop work for night runs and long builds.
steer_which: Which one? Write the word and part of the name: {names}
steer_task_no_text: (a voice note: voice.oga next to this file)
steer_task_done_when: Claude writes the criteria from the text above when the work starts (/nightcall:start).
steer_task_saved: Task saved: {folder}. At the computer: /nightcall:start in that folder - or set steer.py inbox --start to begin at once.
steer_task_started: Task saved and started: {folder}. The board shows how it goes.
steer_no_transcriber: No transcriber on this computer yet: pip install mlx-whisper (Mac) or openai-whisper, or put OPENAI_API_KEY / GROQ_API_KEY in the environment. Meanwhile type the task: task: ...
steer_no_telegram: Set the phone's Telegram first: remote.py telegram --token <bot token> --allow <your Telegram id>.
steer_listening: Listening to the phone: Continue / Stop, "stop", "continue", voice notes and "task: ...".
steer_inbox_set: Tasks from the phone land in {folder}; started at once with: {start}
